title: POC Weekly — Redwood Private VPC pilot sync
topics: Networking: VPC peering, route tables, NAT and egress
Runtime upgrades: CUDA/driver compatibility and inference engine
Performance tuning: batching, KV cache, p95 latency

summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Customer reported intermittent runtime crashes after node kernel upgrades, higher-than-expected p95 latency on larger prompts, and an outstanding egress routing issue with a dependent third-party API. Redwood SE walked through recent telemetry, proposed tuning (batching + cache warmup), and recommended a controlled runtime upgrade path. Next steps: schedule maintenance window for driver/runtime upgrade, share SOC2 + KMS docs, run a targeted benchmark with updated batching config, and follow up on NAT/route fix with cloud infra team.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Meeting type: POC weekly sync — Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem pilot)
Attendees: Sam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Luis Gomez (Redwood CSM); Tom Lee (Atlas ML Eng), Maya Chen (Atlas Infra), Dan Rodriguez (Atlas Security), Rachel Park (Atlas Product)
Shared artifacts: pilot bench: https://redwood.app/atlas/pilot/benchmarks, SOC2 + KMS doc link: https://redwood.app/security/soc2

Summary (auto): quick sync on network egress issue, recent runtime crashes after host upgrades, tuning options for batching and cache warmup, and scheduling a maintenance window for driver/runtime update.

[00:00] Sam Carter: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have the usual suspects, quick roll call — sam here on the AE side, priya from se, luis csm, atlas team?
[00:08] Tom Lee: yeah tom here, maya, dan, rachel — morning / afternoon all, thanks
[00:15] Sam Carter: cool, agenda — 1) network egress bug that blocked the 3rd party ai endpoint, 2) runtime crashes post-kernel upgrade, 3) perf numbers and tuning, 4) schedule upgrade window and next steps
[02:12] Priya Shah: i pulled the telemetry overnight — i'll share screen after — main things: p95 token latency for the long prompt workload is trending ~180-220ms, target was 140-160, so higher than we expected. KV cache hit-rate is around 68% on cold starts, steady-state it goes to 82%, which suggests prefix caching warmup could be improved
[04:30] Maya Chen: quick note on the egress — we changed the route table last week to narrow routes, and it looks like the pilot subnets don't have the correct nat gateway assoc for one of the AZs, so requests to the third-party indexer were intermittently dropping
[05:05] Tom Lee: that matches what we saw — some requests to search-api.thirdparty.com would hang, others fine, so it's intermittent
[06:00] Priya Shah: ok that's network, easy fix — maya, if you can just add the missing nat gateway association for subnet-a and confirm the route table, that should resolve the intermittent egress, and we can re-run the bench
[06:22] Maya Chen: yeah i'll gather the route table screenshots and share; expect to do that today
[07:05] Dan Rodriguez: security question — before any maintenance window to upgrade drivers, we need the KMS rotation schedule and confirmation that the key policy allows the new node identities to access secrets. also i need the SOC2 artifact link for the review
[07:30] Sam Carter: absolutely, we'll share the KMS integration guide and our SOC2 pack. link in chat — also note that for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM options, so you can bring your own keys
[09:12] Priya Shah: back to crashes — we saw 3 OOM-like crashes last night after the infra team applied a host kernel update; stack traces show a driver mismatch: CUDA reported driver 510 while runtime expects 515, so that mismatch can cause model load failures and node restarts
[10:05] Maya Chen: yep we did a host update to 5.10 kernel across the fleet — may have pulled an older nvidia driver image automatically; i think the package curator on our side pinned to a previous driver in the image repo
[11:00] Priya Shah: ok that explains it — remediation path is either roll back the driver or schedule a controlled driver + runtime upgrade. the latter is preferred so we align runtime to the new kernel and test in a canary AZ first
[12:45] Sam Carter: recommended plan: 1) smoke canary with 1 node in AZ-b, 2) run the bench with priya's config, 3) monitor kv cache metrics and p95 for 1 hour, 4) roll to remaining nodes if stable. propose window 2025-08-12 02:00-04:00 UTC
[13:20] Rachel Park: is that during our low traffic window? yes that's fine for us but need to confirm product acceptance tests pass
[14:00] Priya Shah: on tuning — primary knobs: batch size target, max latency bucket, and cache TTL/prime behavior. for long prompts we suggest reducing max batch latency to 12ms and increasing per-request batch token cap to 96 for better throughput without hurting p95. also pre-warm KV cache on common prefixes we saw in your dataset
[15:45] Tom Lee: can you quantify the expected improvement? even roughs
[16:05] Priya Shah: in our lab runs that config dropped p95 from ~210ms to ~150-160ms on the 8k token workload, throughput increased about 1.2x. caveat: numbers depend on prompt distribution and model quantization — your current pilot is running the 4-bit qpe variant which helps cost but can widen latency sometimes
[17:30] Tom Lee: interesting, we are on that 4-bit qpe — could we punt to 8-bit for the canary? maybe trade cost for latency to validate
[17:55] Priya Shah: yep canary can run an 8-bit variant for a subset of requests; we can route a canary tag to that variant and fallback automatically if latency regresses. cost delta will be small for the short window
[19:10] Luis Gomez: i'll document the routing rule in the playbook and share the canary routing config
[20:00] Maya Chen: one more infra question — how do we handle private repo images for the runtime? our security policy requires images come from our private registry and be scanned
[20:22] Sam Carter: we support customer registry images. Priya will provide the runtime image manifest and a small Dockerfile so your infra can build and scan; we also support signed images via cosign
[21:45] Dan Rodriguez: KMS again — when you say customer-managed KMS, do we need to rotate keys before the upgrade? rotation may cause brief token re-auth if not careful
[22:05] Sam Carter: no forced rotation required; we just need a service account principal added to the key policy so new nodes can decrypt model keys. Priya will share exact IAM bindings
[23:50] Priya Shah: i'll attach the IAM snippet and the cosign verification steps to the ticket
[25:10] Tom Lee: any known regressions after driver updates historically? we want to avoid surprises
[25:30] Priya Shah: occasional driver/runtime mismatches, yes — that's why canary + health checks are important. we also keep an automatic model fallback in the routing policy so if a node fails to load a quantized variant we can fallback to another compatible instance
[27:05] Sam Carter: small note on telemetry — please enable the debug trace for the model load path during the canary so we can capture any failures. that adds a small overhead but helps root cause
[29:00] Maya Chen: on the nat fix, once i push the route table update, how quickly can you confirm? will you re-run bench right away?
[29:18] Priya Shah: we can trigger a smoke benchmark within 15 minutes of confirmation. bench script will run three iterations and upload traces to the shared bucket
[31:40] Tom Lee: about logging — can we get request-level logs obfuscated for pii but with correlation ids so our devs can trace issues without exposing patient data
[32:05] Sam Carter: yep we support token-level obfuscation and can emit correlation IDs as part of the structured logs; we will share the log schema
[33:50] Priya Shah: small callout on cache TTLs — you had TTL of 10m, i recommend lowering to 2m for this workload to reduce stale prefix behavior — but if your workload has very long repeated prefixes we can bump it back after observing
[35:15] Rachel Park: will that increase egress to your model repo or storage tier? need to be mindful of cross-account egress costs
[35:35] Priya Shah: modest increase but within pilot envelope. we'll estimate token-level cost in the bench report
[36:50] Luis Gomez: i've updated the playbook with the proposed tuning and the rollback steps; sharing shortly
[38:02] Maya Chen: i pushed the route table screenshots to the ticket and updated the NAT association — i can confirm connectivity to the third party now, i see 200s on the api
[38:22] Tom Lee: perfect, can you share the exact test url and we will validate from our side
[38:35] Maya Chen: posted in the chat — test endpoint is https://search-api.thirdparty.com/health
[40:00] Priya Shah: ok next actions recap — priyash to share bench script and tuning config, sam to share pricing & soc2 link, maya to confirm routing, dan to list compliance artifacts, luis to schedule maintenance window
[41:10] Dan Rodriguez: i'll send the compliance checklist by friday, includes KMS acceptance tests and network diagrams
[42:30] Sam Carter: i'll send calendar invite for proposed 2025-08-12 02-04 UTC; if that conflicts we can shift +/- 24 hours. thanks all — any final q's?
[43:05] Tom Lee: none here, thanks
[43:12] Rachel Park: thanks everyone
[44:00] Sam Carter: thanks, we will follow up with the artifacts and see you next week for the post-canary review
